header: ANSWER FIRST, SOURCES AFTER. When a question is answered by text in the stored documents (circulars, holiday policy notes, announcements), I want the person to see the ANSWER first, as clear FACTS (a small table, or one key figure), and, for accountability, the document it came from with the exact words that prove it. This module is GENERIC: it knows nothing about any particular circular. It
2. asks the model for FACTS, each with a verbatim quote (buildAnswerPrompt, parseModelAnswer),
3. REFUSES to show anything the text does not prove (verifyAnswer).
I never trust the model. An answer is shown only when ALL of these hold, for EVERY row (label | value) of the answer:
- its quote is found, word for word (ignoring spaces, case and punctuation), in the passage it names;
- the value's numbers and words are all inside that quote (nothing added, nothing calculated);
- the label's words are inside that quote, so a value can never sit under another row's label;

- a number taken from a TABLE ROW (a quote with five or more numbers) must come with its COLUMN label, and that label must stand right next to the number in the quote ("Wages Per Day: 808"). A total, or any other column, can therefore never be passed off as the figure asked for (this is the mistake that put "Rs 20995.30 per day" on screen on 17 Oct: a monthly total);
- words like "daily" or "monthly" in the title or note are backed by a column that says so;
- every number in the title and note is in a quote or in the cited document's own title or date.

If any rule fails, no answer is shown and the person sees the matching documents exactly as before. My rule: "a right answer or an honest 'not found', never a confident wrong one". If the stored text of a scan is damaged (a lost column, a garbled number) the rules fail, so a damaged scan gives NO answer, never a wrong one. This file is pure (no database, no network) and is unit-tested by circularAnswer.selftest.ts. The model call is passed in (an LlmFn).

symbols.sig: function columnBesideValue(nq: string, column: string, value: string, allowBefore: boolean): boolean
doc: True if the column label stands right next to the value in the quote. In a table row ("TOTAL: 20995.30 | Wages Per Day: 808") a value belongs to the label BEFORE it, never to the label after it, so there I require the value to FOLLOW its column label (`allowBefore` false). In a sentence ("Four (04) days Casual Leave") the value may come before the label.

symbols.name: piecesInOneRow
symbols.sig: export function piecesInOneRow(quote: string, passageText: string): boolean
doc: A quote that leaves cells out. A model asked for "the label, the column and the value together" often copies only those cells ("Area: WORKS | Daily Wages (Rs. Per Day of duty): 808"), or marks what it left out with "...". I accept that when every piece (cells split at "|" and at an ellipsis) is found word for word in the document, IN ORDER, within ONE table row: the span from the first piece to the last must be short and must not hold the same column label twice, because that would be two rows and a label could end up beside another row's value.

symbols.name: sentenceWordsAround
symbols.sig: export function sentenceWordsAround(passageText: string, quote: string): Set<string>
doc: Returns the words of the SENTENCE of the document that holds the quote. A model often quotes only a clause (`may please be read as "Rs.14,999/-"`), whose subject ("the amount of the Gift Card") stands earlier in the same sentence. I let the sentence run back to the previous full stop followed by a space (or line break) and forward to the next one, at most 400 characters either way; "Rs.15,000" and "w.e.f." do not end a sentence (no space after the dot). ONLY PROSE QUALIFIES: the result is empty if the quote cannot be located, if a real sentence boundary is not found on BOTH sides within 400 characters (a table, flattened to one run of text, has none: its heading must never back a value of another column), or if the window holds a table cell separator ("|") or a table marker.

Per Day of duty)") or reorder it ("Wages per day"), but every word it names must be in the label of THE SAME cell as the value. That way a value can never be passed off under another column's label (a total is not a daily wage).

symbols.name: snapQuote
symbols.sig: export function snapQuote(p: Passage, r: RowIn): string | null
doc: THE QUOTE AS A POINTER. A model's quote is often not a copy (cells left out, a clause, a few words changed). What has to be proved is the fact, so I look the value up in the document and take the document's own words around it; I accept the model's quote as a pointer to that place only if at least SNAP_MIN_OVERLAP of its own words stand in those surroundings (a value quoted from the wrong place has few of them there). Returns the document's words (word for word by construction), or null.

symbols.name: tidyAnswer
symbols.sig: function tidyAnswer(a: ModelAnswer): ModelAnswer
doc: I repair the presentation instead of refusing: a long heading or label is shortened, a long note without a sentence end is dropped, extra rows are cut.

symbols.name: confirmationRefusal
symbols.sig: function confirmationRefusal(p: Passage, value: string, quote: string): string | null
doc: THE CONFIRMATION GATE. For a page that a second reader checked, a number of the answer's VALUE that only the pipeline's reading had is not confirmed (it may be a misreading: a rupee sign read as a "2" turned "(Rs 15,000)" into "215,000"), so I refuse the answer. A number that both readings had, a number on a page that was never checked, and a value with no digits are not affected. The pages are those that hold the quote (its longest piece, when the quote leaves cells out). When a row was cut by a chunk break and the quote is in no single part, every page of the passage counts, and a number only counts as unconfirmed if NO page confirms it.

symbols.name: tidyInfographicDebris
symbols.sig: export function tidyInfographicDebris(sentence: string): string
doc: A note is the model's PARAPHRASE, and a paraphrase can drop a limit ("entitlement of CASUAL leave is calculated proportionately" became "Entitlement is calculated proportionately"). So I show a note only as the document's OWN sentence: the sentence of the cited passages that holds at least 60% of the note's words (word stems), cut at a word. If no sentence does, the note is dropped (the facts stay). WHAT AN INFOGRAPHIC LEAVES IN THE TEXT. A page that is a picture with words on it (a numbered procedure with a stopwatch and a sample code) is read word by word, so the numbers of its steps, its sample code and its timer come out among the sentences: "OTP 123456 1 2 Both OTPs are required to be shared ... five minutes. - 05:00 - 3 Video verification ...". I clean the sentence shown to the reader of exactly that, and of nothing else (what is left is still the document's own words, in order):

* at the START: the words before the first word that has a lower-case letter are dropped when they hold a lone one- or two-digit number (a step's number) or a number of five digits or more (a sample code): "OTP 123456 1 2 Both OTPs ..." -> "Both OTPs ..."; "TRINETRA Cyber Security ..." and "PF 2024 rules" are left alone (an acronym, a year);
* at the END: from a timer ("- 05:00 -") on, the rest is the next step of the picture.
I do not clean when that would leave less than a sentence.

symbols.sig: const UNIT_WORDS = new Set( ("second seconds sec secs minute minutes min mins hour hours hr hrs day days week weeks month months year yea …
doc: THE UNIT OF A BARE NUMBER, for the big figure of the answer: "15" under "Account locked duration" means nothing without "minutes". The model is told to give the value without units (a unit it adds on its own, or a "per day" the document never printed, is a made-up fact), and that rule stays. After the answer has been verified, I show the figure with the unit the DOCUMENT prints right after that number in the verified quote: "15 minutes", "8 characters", "90 days", "5%", "Rs. 15,000". This applies only to a whole bare number, only to a unit from a fixed list of real units (not any word that follows: "51 dated" is not a unit), only when every place the number stands in the quote gives the same unit (otherwise the figure is shown as it is). The value that was verified is never changed, only the words shown with it.
